name: matmul-cpu (core_v5 GEMM kernels)
workload: Single-precision GEMM M=N=K=4096, 24 threads, AVX-512 14x32 micro-kernel, 10 timed rounds after 2 warmups
claimed_speedup: Multi-core peak 2010.61 vs OpenBLAS 1914.91 GFLOPS (~106% of OpenBLAS); single-core 110.74 vs 132.88 GFLOPS (82.4%, slower)
hardware: Intel Xeon Silver 4310 @ 2.10GHz, 24 cores, 2 sockets, AVX-512
tradeoffs: Only C=A*B^T+C row-major sgemm; not a full BLAS; tile sizes tuned to one CPU.
caveats: Compiler and flags not stated in README (xmake build); no license file seen; wins only multithreaded at 4096 and loses single-core to OpenBLAS; first-party numbers.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ GEMM matrix multiply library faster than OpenBLAS MKL benchmark GFLOPS github (outperforms query)

name: sgemm.c (salykova)
workload: FP32 GEMM on square sizes, multithreaded and single-threaded, AVX2/FMA3 BLIS-style kernel via OpenMP
claimed_speedup: README: 'performance comparable to modern BLAS libraries'; plots vs OpenBLAS only, no numeric table; blog's author claims parity or better against OpenBLAS/MKL on the tuned CPUs
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X and Intel Core Ultra 265 @ 90W, DDR5
tradeoffs: FP32 only, no AVX-512, tile sizes and threading tuned to two specific CPUs; not a full BLAS API.
caveats: Results are graphs, no numbers in text; 'comparable' rather than clearly faster; blog benchmark page https://salykova.github.io/matmul-cpu; a third-party reproduction (matmul-cpu repo) found the reference underperforms OpenBLAS on a Xeon.

name: Optimizing-DGEMM-on-Intel-CPUs-with-AVX512F
workload: Stepwise DGEMM kernels (19 versions) on square matrices; single-thread kernel 18 and multithreaded kernel 19
claimed_speedup: Single-thread kernel 18 ~120 GFLOPS of 128 GFLOPS peak, comparable to MKL; kernel 19 surpasses MKL under multithreading (no table in text)
hardware: Intel Xeon W-2255 (2 AVX-512 units, 3.7 GHz base, 4.0 GHz AVX-512 turbo)
tradeoffs: DGEMM only, C with inline assembly, tuned to AVX-512 Xeon; GPL-3.0 copyleft.
caveats: First-party; MKL beta version; multithread win shown in plot not text numbers; compile flags not confirmed.
found_via: GitHub topic blas (C++ filter) page listing

name: LibShalom
baseline: OpenBLAS, BLIS, ARMPL, BLASFEO, LIBXSMM (small/irregular GEMM)
workload: Small (8x8x8 to 128x128x128) and irregular-shaped SGEMM/DGEMM on ARMv8, plus VGG CNN layers and CP2K 5x5x5 kernels
claimed_speedup: Up to 2x vs BLASFEO on 8x8x8; 1.8x average vs BLIS on irregular GEMMs (second-best); 1.05-2x vs OpenBLAS; up to 2x vs LIBXSMM on CP2K 5x5x5; up to 4x on some VGG layers
tradeoffs: ARMv8 only, assembly kernels, small sgemm/dgemm API (not full BLAS); GCC>=8.2 and OpenMP.
caveats: SC21 paper (peer-reviewed); repo owner is 'AnonymousYWL' and a mirror MYLIB lists MIT; repo README lists no numbers; MKL not a baseline (ARM); last commit date not retrieved.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ GEMM ... GFLOPS; LibShalom paper and repo

name: BLASFEO
baseline: Intel MKL and OpenBLAS (level-3 BLAS and LAPACK routines on small matrices)
workload: Cache-resident small dense matrices (up to ~100-256): gemm_nt and potrf_l in double and single precision
claimed_speedup: 20-30% faster than level-3 BLAS (MKL) for matrices up to 100; 2-3x faster than corresponding LAPACK routines; potrf_l ~2-3x vs OpenBLAS/MKL; Cortex A15 sp potrf_l 4-5x vs OpenBLAS
hardware: Intel Core i7 4800MQ (Haswell, 3.3 GHz, 52.8 Gflops peak); also Ivy Bridge i3 3520M, Cortex A57/A15
tradeoffs: Panel-major storage in native API (BLAS API wrapper also available); optimized for small cache-resident matrices, not large.
caveats: Numbers are from the 2017 arXiv paper (older MKL/OpenBLAS versions); the repo has no benchmark table, see blasfeo.syscop.de; hardware old.
found_via: WebSearch: github small GEMM JIT library faster than MKL OpenBLAS libxsmm OR BLASFEO

name: LIBXSMM
workload: Small dense/sparse matrix multiplication via runtime code generation (JIT)
claimed_speedup: No numbers verified on opened pages; docs defer to a 'results' branch and the SC16 paper (not opened, 403)
stars_or_usage: 977 stars; used in CP2K, SeisSol, Nek5000, PyTorch extensions
tradeoffs: Targets small matrices; Intel and ARM JIT backends; v2.0 focused on Tensor Processing Primitives.
caveats: Widely referenced as a fast MKL alternative for small GEMM but no numeric claim was confirmed this session; LibShalom paper cites it as slower than LibShalom on ARM.
found_via: WebSearch: github small GEMM JIT library faster than MKL ...
